The '''2023–24 Danish Superliga''' (officially the '''3F Superliga''' for sponsorship purposes) was the 34th season of the [[Danish Superliga]].

It began on 21 July 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title= {{!}} Nyheder |url=https://superliga.dk/nyheder/kamptidspunkter/datoplanen-for-saesonen-2023-24-er-klar |access-date=2023-05-28 |website=superliga.dk |language=da-DK}}</ref>

==Teams==

[[Vejle Boldklub]] won the [[2022–23 Danish 1st Division]] and made an immediate return to top flight,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hvidovre rykker i Superligaen efter Sønderjyske-dukkert {{!}} Nyheder |url=https://jyllands-posten.dk/sport/fodbold/ECE15910312/hvidovre-rykker-i-superligaen-efter-soenderjyskedukkert/ |access-date=2023-05-29 |website=jyllands-posten |date=28 May 2023 |language=da-DK}}</ref> while [[Hvidovre IF]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hvidovre IF rykker op i Superligaen {{!}} Nyheder |url=https://ekstrabladet.dk/sport/fodbold/dansk_fodbold/hvidovre-if-rykker-op-i-superligaen/9785267 |access-date=2023-05-29 |website=ekstrabladet |date=28 May 2023 |language=da-DK}}</ref> secured 2nd place and will play in the first tier division for the first time since [[1996–97 Danish Superliga|1997]]. The two teams replaced [[AC Horsens]] and [[AaB Fodbold|AaB]], making it the first time since 1986 that [[AaB Fodbold|AaB]] would not play in the top tier division.

==European play-offs==
The 3rd-placed team of the championship round advances to a play-off match against the winning team of the qualification round (no. 7) in a single-leg tie, with the team from the championship round as hosts. The winner earns a place in the [[2024–25 UEFA Conference League#Second qualifying round|Conference League second qualifying round]].
